generator.program.note: The program the authors chose to grow this taxon's rosette succulent species (named in each species' spec until G2.3a moved it here).

traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 229, 505: Simpson (Asphodelaceae s.s.) calls the flowers hypogynous. Simpson p. 505 defines hypogynous and epigynous as flowers without a hypanthium. Hemerocallidaceae and Xanthorrhoeaceae, which APG adds, are not described.

traits.note: VicFlora's account of the family, as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): flowers actinomorphic or rarely slightly zygomorphic; tepals 6, free or fused, in 2 whorls of 3; stamens 6 in 2 whorls of 3, mostly hypogynous; ovary superior, carpels as many as the perianth whorl (Watson and Dallwitz) and fused (Hortflora).

traits.leaf_division.note: Hutchinson (vol. 2, 2nd ed., 1959), family 372 Liliaceae, whose asphodels, aloes and day-lilies APG puts in Asphodelaceae: leaves simple, in a basal tuft or rosette; fruit mostly a capsule opening along its cells, rarely a berry.

traits.fruit_type.note: Hutchinson (vol. 2, 2nd ed., 1959), family 372 Liliaceae, whose asphodels, aloes and day-lilies APG puts in Asphodelaceae: leaves simple, in a basal tuft or rosette; fruit mostly a capsule opening along its cells, rarely a berry.

traits.rosette.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Asphodelaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Xeronemataceae: whether the leaves gather in rosettes (character 22), coded usually a basal rosette, sometimes no rosette, sometimes rosettes at the stem tips. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.life_span.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Asphodelaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Xeronemataceae: the herbs' life form (character 21), coded perennial. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 229, 230, family Asphodelaceae: phyllotaxis pattern spiral to distichous, usually; read as {"distichous": "often", "spiral": "often"}.

traits.leaf_venation.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 229, 230, family Asphodelaceae: leaf venation parallel; read as "parallel".

traits.leaf_margin.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 229, 230, family Asphodelaceae: leaf margin entire to toothed or spiny, often; read as {"entire": "often", "spiny": "often"}.

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 229, 230, family Asphodelaceae: inflorescence raceme or panicle; read as {"panicle": "often", "raceme": "often"}.

traits.perennation.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Asphodelaceae, with the parts of Asphodelaceae it codes as families of their own (Phormiaceae), whose further states read as sometimes: how its perennial herbs last from year to year (character 25), coded often a rhizome, often pseudobulbs; with them, often a rhizome, often pseudobulbs, sometimes tubers. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 25 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add zygomorphic (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 229, 230: actinomorphic or zygomorphic.
